key_points: BPC segment grew 27% YoY to Rs91bn in FY26, maintaining three consecutive years of >27% GMV growth with 42mn+ customer base
Fashion segment turned profitable with 0.3% EBITDA margin in Q4FY26 vs -10.2% in Q4FY25, achieving Rs49.5bn GMV at 30% YoY growth
House of Nykaa portfolio NSV reached Rs17bn in FY26 (50% CAGR from FY23), targeting Rs51bn by FY30e with Dot & Key contributing 59% at 128% CAGR
Physical footprint expanded to 338 stores across 100 cities, serving as customer acquisition funnel for premium beauty segment
Consolidated revenues crossed Rs100bn in FY26 with EBITDA margins expanding from 6.0% (FY25) to 7.5%, projected to reach 11.4% by FY29e
catalysts: Fashion segment achieving sustainable profitability and scale
House of Nykaa portfolio expansion into new categories (clinical body care, premium fragrance, nutraceuticals)
Store network expansion and omnichannel integration
Margin expansion from operating leverage in BPC segment
Online BPC market projected to reach Rs1.3trln by FY31e (vs Rs570bn in FY26)
reports.summary: Nykaa initiated with BUY rating and 12-month target price of Rs400 (50x FY29e EBITDA). The company is experiencing an earnings inflection driven by BPC segment resilience and fashion segment breakeven, with core beauty growing at 31% CAGR while House of Nykaa scaled 50% CAGR. Consolidated EBITDA margins are expanding from 7.5% to projected 11.4% by FY29e, supported by premiumization and improving unit economics across both segments.
reports.connection_narrative: India's beauty and personal care market is structurally shifting from offline to online and unorganized to organized retail, with online BPC penetration growing at 30% CAGR to reach Rs1.3trln by FY31e—more than 1.5x the pace of overall BPC market growth. Simultaneously, India's fashion market is projected to become the world's third-largest by FY31e, with online fashion accelerating at 22-25% CAGR. These secular tailwinds are being turbocharged by rising incomes driving premiumization, with India's lifestyle shopper base now at 220 million consumers seeking quality over discounts. Nykaa is uniquely positioned to capture this dual growth opportunity through its differentiated dual-engine strategy. In BPC, Nykaa's 42-million-strong customer ecosystem and 27% GMV growth significantly outpaces the 9% overall market growth, demonstrating category leadership through exclusive brand partnerships and premium curation. The company's owned brands portfolio, anchored by Dot & Key which has compounded at 128% CAGR to Rs10bn NSV, is generating high-teen EBITDA margins and shifting the consolidated margin profile upward. In fashion, Nykaa has decisively rejected the discount-led race to scale pursued by competitors like Myntra and Ajio, instead building a premium curation-focused marketplace with customers spending 60% more per order and holding 70% higher new-season inventory than competitors, which has miraculously turned the segment profitable in Q4FY26 after two years of losses. The company's 338-store omnichannel footprint across 100 cities serves as a critical customer acquisition funnel and trust builder for premium beauty, directly addressing the organized offline market opportunity worth Rs1.2trln by FY31e. The single most important catalyst to watch is whether Nykaa Fashion can sustain its mid-50s NSV growth momentum and maintain profitability as it scales toward 4% market share by FY29e, which would unlock a multi-billion rupee profit pool in a Rs4.5trln online fashion market. The key risk is discretionary spend slowdown in the premium segment if consumer confidence deteriorates, combined with intensifying competition from deep-pocketed incumbents like Reliance-backed Tira who can leverage their conglomerate distribution and scale.
